title: Multi-tenant latency & error-budget scope with staged rollback playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: PRD summary: Define a single, auditable SLO contract and staged rollback/playbook for multi-tenant chat and short-form generation routes. This ticket captures requirements clarifications, scope boundaries, acceptance criteria, and rollout gates for a first-pass operational contract that will be enforced by dashboarding, automated burn-rate monitors, and canary traffic controls. Goal: enable predictable per-tenant experience while providing safe automated rollback for model or config rollouts that materially increase latency or error rates. This is explicitly scoped to hosted API chat and completion endpoints (non-streaming 1-token-per-request flows and streaming 1st-token latency constraints are handled by a follow-up), excludes embeddings and vector service endpoints.
requirements_clarifications: SLO windows: rolling 7-day for error budget accounting; 30-day for contractual reporting (billing/SLA).

Latency targets: p50/p90/p99 for text-generation (short prompts <512 tokens) and chat streaming first-token (p50/p90). For this ticket we focus on non-stream p50=60ms, p90=220ms, p99=520ms on dedicated tier; hosted will have relaxed tiers per region.
Uptime target: 99.95% monthly availability for API ingress per region for these routes.

Error budget definition: errors defined as 5xx and model-level timeouts; client-side cancels excluded. Budget is allowable 0.05% monthly error rate as primary contract, with staged conservative gates during rollout.
Per-tenant measurement: compute weighted SLOs per tenant by request volume; can apply floor on low-traffic tenants (min sample threshold = 1000 requests/week) before enforcement.

Metric sources: primary source is request-level telemetry emitted by runtime (trace id + route + model + latency_ms + status). Alerting and burn-rate calculation must use the aggregated metrics in the platform metrics pipeline (metrics.redwood.prod).
scope_changes: Initial PRD included streaming-first-token SLOs; removed from scope to reduce rollout blast radius. Separate ticket to cover streaming.
Added per-tenant minimum sample floor after PM/Eng sync on 2025-02-18 to avoid noisy enforcement for very small customers.
Excluded embeddings and vector search from enforcement in this ticket per Eng capacity planning (will be added in a later phase).
acceptance_criteria: A1: Metrics pipeline publishes per-route p50/p90/p99 and error-rate at 5m and 1h windows into the SLO dashboard.
A2: Definition page in Confluence (linked) describing calculation formulas, windows, and edge-cases published and reviewed by SRE and Runtime owners.
A3: Automated burn-rate monitor that calculates 7-day rolling burn and raises critical incident when projected monthly burn > 50% within next 6h is deployed and tested in staging.

A4: Canary rollout policy implemented: start at 2% traffic for 1h, if no critical alerts and burn < 10% of allowance, increase to 10% for 3h; if criteria met, proceed to 50% then 100% per schedule. Automated rollback triggers if sustained burn-rate breach or p99 increase > 2x baseline over 1h.
A5: Runbook created and validated with on-call SREs including steps to manually abort rollouts, pin model version, and emergency throttling.
A6: End-to-end test in staging that simulates an injected latency regression and confirms rollback triggers and notification routing (PagerDuty + slack #sre).
A7: Product & Legal sign-off on SLA language for customer-facing docs referencing 99.95% availability and error budget policies.
rollout_gates: Gate 0 (Preflight): telemetry coverage validated for 72h in staging; no missing fields.
Gate 1 (Canary 2% / 1h): fail if critical alerts fire or 1h observed burn-rate projection > 25% of monthly allowance.
Gate 2 (10% / 3h): fail if p99 latency increases > 1.5x baseline or burn-rate projection > 25% for any tenant with >1% traffic share.
Gate 3 (50%): require SRE-reviewed post-canary report and no unresolved incidents; automated rollback if any tenant-level burn > 40% in 2h window.
Gate 4 (100%): only after 24h at 50% with sustained metrics within targets.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: per-route latency histograms, error-rate heatmaps, top-10 tenants by burn-rate. Template dashboard link: https://dashboards.redwood.prod/slo/pm-16209
Alerts: critical (pager) on projected monthly burn > 50% within 6h; high (slack) on sustained p99 > threshold for 15m; medium (email) on missing telemetry payloads.
Audit logs: all rollouts and automated rollback actions recorded with model version and canary percent.
implementation_notes: Owners: PM=Aisha Patel, Eng=Marco Reyes, SRE=Jin-Ho Kim, DX=Rina Bose.
Required infra: metrics schema update (ENG-4821), automation playbook for canary orchestration (ENG-9972), dashboard template PR: github.com/redwood/platform/pulls/7812.
Fallbacks: if automated rollback fails, manual pin to previous model and emergency throttling controlled via console feature flag.

decision_log: Decision 2025-02-18: Remove streaming-first-token from this ticket to limit risk (agreed by PM+Eng).
Decision 2025-02-20: Use 7-day rolling window for operational burn-rate and 30-day for contractual reporting.
Decision 2025-02-24: Adopt per-tenant sample floor of 1000 req/week to avoid noisy enforcement.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Small tenants could be unfairly impacted by noisy metrics. Mitigation: apply sample floor and per-tenant smoothing of p99 using a 1h rolling average.
Risk: Automated rollback could oscillate in presence of transient network flaps. Mitigation: require at least two successive windows triggering rollback criteria and attach cooldown (1h).
Risk: Missing telemetry fields during rollout. Mitigation: preflight tests and fallback to region-level enforcement if tenant-level data missing.
test_plan: Unit tests for burn-rate calculation with synthetic incidents.
Staging injection test: simulate 10% latency regression and verify rollback automation triggers.
Canary rehearsal in low-traffic region (EU-west-2) to validate alerting and audit logs.
